correctness.rationale: For three independent eccentric-anomaly parameters, the exact chord vector factorization gives absolute slope epsilon |cot((theta+phi)/2)|. If all three triangle angles are below fixed beta>pi/2, one chord must be steeper than tan((pi-beta)/2); away from O(epsilon^2) endpoint/overlap sets this localizes a unique reflected pair with theta_i+theta_j=2pi+epsilon h. On that band the short chord is epsilon sin(theta_i)(h,-2)+O(epsilon^2), the third chord is predominantly horizontal, and the limiting angle condition is |h|<2kappa with kappa=-cot(beta). The angular pair limit is {pi/2 +/- atan(h/2)}. Independent uniform parameter measure has Jacobian epsilon, giving per-pair 2kappa epsilon/pi and total 6kappa epsilon/pi. Dominated convergence of the band indicator, negligible overlaps, and Scheffe convergence after normalization imply the claimed independent pair/angle/uniform-h marked total-variation law for every fixed beta in (pi/2,pi). I separately implemented direct Euclidean-angle QMC with importance samples at beta=120 degrees: P(epsilon)/epsilon was 1.2247 at 0.025 and 1.1406 at 0.005, trending toward exact 2sqrt(3)/pi=1.10266 (finite-aspect deviation explicitly retained).
